about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (ECHO)
channels.note: EPA's sewer overflow and bypass event tables (NPDES electronic reporting): Mississippi permittees file their 5-day reports through NeT-SewerOverflow and EPA publishes them daily (358 Mississippi reports from 47 permits in the 2026-11-04 extract; median 4 days from start to receipt). The only statewide dated record: it covers every operator in the state, public or private. (research/ms/report.md §2.2)

channels.name: City of Jackson (sewer system run by JXN Water)
channels.legal_basis: United States and State of Mississippi v. City of Jackson (S.D. Miss.): the 2013 consent decree's Sewer Overflow Response Plan calls for a news release and temporary signs for significant overflows (as reported in the press; the plan was not read)
channels.note: JXN Water's news page (answered 200 on 2026-11-07), where the overflow response plan's news releases for significant overflows would appear; whether they are posted here was not checked. (ms-jxn-water)

channels.name: City of Jackson (sewer system run by JXN Water)
channels.legal_basis: United States and State of Mississippi v. City of Jackson (S.D. Miss.): the 2013 consent decree's Sewer Overflow Response Plan calls for a news release and temporary signs for significant overflows (as reported in the press; the plan was not read)
channels.note: No web form: temporary signs at significant overflows under the overflow response plan. On site only.

channels.name: City of Jackson (sewer system run by JXN Water)
channels.legal_basis: United States v. City of Jackson (S.D. Miss.), 2023 interim stipulated order: JXN Water, the interim third-party manager, files quarterly status reports with the court (as reported; the order was not read)
channels.note: No URL known: JXN Water's quarterly status reports to the court give the period's overflow totals; no page listing them was found (jxnwater.com/reports answered 404 on 2026-11-07). (ms-jxn-water)

channels.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (Beach Monitoring Program)
channels.legal_basis: BEACH Act of 2000 (33 U.S.C. 1346): a state beach program funded under it notifies the public of exceedances of the bacteria criteria; MDEQ's Beach Monitoring Program, with the University of Southern Mississippi's Gulf Coast Research Laboratory (statute text not quoted)
channels.note: The layer behind beaches.mdeq.ms.gov: 21 Gulf Coast stations, each with an advisory flag, a closure flag, the event type (Enterococci, HAB, debris), MDEQ's start date and the advisory or closure text. MDEQ posts advisories here first; since 2026-09-08 routine advisories go only here and to beach signs. None in effect on 2026-11-07. Read hourly by the feed (both flags, MDEQ's start date, the station's point). (ms-mdeq-beach-monitoring)

channels.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (Beach Monitoring Program)
channels.legal_basis: BEACH Act of 2000 (33 U.S.C. 1346): a state beach program funded under it notifies the public of exceedances of the bacteria criteria; MDEQ's Beach Monitoring Program, with the University of Southern Mississippi's Gulf Coast Research Laboratory (statute text not quoted)
channels.note: No web form: signs posted at the beach segments under advisory. From 2026-09-08 routine beach advisories are "communicated through posted beach signage and the MDEQ Beach Monitoring website rather than text alerts and news releases" (MDEQ news release, 2026-09-08). On site only.

channels.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (Beach Monitoring Program)
channels.note: No web form: the text alerts (text "MDEQbeach" to 95577) and the e-mail list that carried beach advisories ended with routine advisories on 2026-09-08 (MDEQ news release of that day). Kept as a row so the retired channel stays on record; no web channel found for it. Voluntary. (ms-mdeq-beach-alerts)

channels.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality
channels.note: MDEQ's news releases (RSS, answered 200 on 2026-11-07). Ad hoc water contact advisories after sewage discharges come this way: 2026-09-02, an advisory for an unnamed tributary of Trahon Creek and Trahon Creek to the Pearl River "due to an ongoing sewage bypass", the release adding that "the longstanding water contact advisory for the section of the Pearl River from Hanging Moss Creek to the Byram Swinging bridge remains in effect". Beach advisories came this way until 2026-09-07. No law requires the releases. Read by the feed: an issue opens an advisory, a lift ends it, and the Pearl River advisory the release cites is a record of its own. (ms-mdeq-water-contact-advisories)

channels.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality
channels.legal_basis: MDEQ, Reporting Sanitary Sewer Overflows or Bypasses in Mississippi (NeT-SewerOverflow flyer): "Municipal and private sanitary sewer collection and treatment providers in Mississippi must report sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) and/or bypasses to the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) within 24 hours of the event. ... Starting December 21, 2025, in addition to the 24-hr reporting requirement, an electronic report shall be submitted to the MDEQ within 5 days ... through NeT-SewerOverflow"; NPDES permit conditions (40 CFR 122.41(l)(6))
channels.note: No web form: every permittee, public or private, reports a sanitary sewer overflow or bypass to MDEQ within 24 hours (telephone, e-mail or voicemail after hours) and files the 5-day report through EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow; no Mississippi statute or rule requiring the public to be told was found, and MDEQ posts no list or map of the reports. No web channel found; they reach the public through EPA's tables days later. (research/ms/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Pearl Riverkeeper
channels.note: The watershed group for the Pearl River; the press reports it petitioned MDEQ to enforce the notice in Jackson's overflow response plan (date not confirmed). Answered 200 on 2026-11-07; content not traced beyond the home page. Voluntary. (research/ms/profile.json)

channels.name: Swim Drink Fish
channels.note: Swim Guide (a script app); the research found no Mississippi listing (research/ms/profile.json, swim_guide false). Voluntary; no API.
channels.barrier_review: an app only (Swim Guide): no web page of its own, but no login wall either
